why: Single source of truth for main's required status-check contexts. scripts/ci/assert-repo-policy.sh reads it and asserts that the live branch rules for main (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/rules/branches/main, which is ruleset `main founder-bypass` today) require exactly these — in both directions, so a context here that GitHub does not require and a context GitHub requires that is missing here both fail. Keeping the list in one file is the F-1135 lesson applied to CI contexts: a second hand-maintained copy goes stale while still looking like something is watching. A `branch` key used to sit here and nothing read it — the branch comes from POLICY_BRANCH, defaulting to main — so it was a third copy of a fact that could disagree with the other two, and it is gone.
note: These are job NAMES as GitHub renders them on a commit's check-runs: `typecheck-test` (ci.yml), `gitleaks + trufflehog` (secret-scan.yml), `dependency review` (dependency-review.yml). Renaming a job renames its context and silently drops the required check — change this file in the same PR.
